input: # leniency.tsv - jsonic base leniency must NOT leak through the CSS plugin.
# dialect, and across the tabnas grammar plugins its base leniency leaking
# through a plugin has been the single largest source of over-acceptance
# (@tabnas/json5 rejects '{a:1' with the plugin alone but ACCEPTS it on the
# documented stack). None of the documents below is CSS, so a CSS parser must
# reject every one of them, on either configuration.
# ts/test/leniency.test.ts additionally asserts the stronger EQUIVALENCE
# property: the documented stack and 'new Tabnas().use(Css)' (no jsonic)
# NOT a probe: 'a:{b:1}'. It looks like a jsonic object but it is also a
# perfectly well-formed CSS qualified rule (selector 'a:', block '{b:1}'),
# and this plugin parses it as one. A fixture demanding ERROR there would be
# a FALSE oracle, not a real conformance gap.
# The brace-first documents below ('{a:1}', '{"a":1}', '{}') are a genuine
# disagreement between the two authorities this repo measures against: CSS
# Syntax L3 accepts them as a qualified rule with an EMPTY prelude, while
# reworkcss/css -- the AST model README.md claims -- throws "selector
# missing". This plugin follows reworkcss, so ERROR is the expectation here.
